checks.check: required functions exist in the exact linked candidate
first-party start brackets vendor start with IRQ save/restore
IRQ primitives are real clri/seti instructions
switch tables are identified rather than disassembled as instructions
16 kHz selector reaches the expected oversampling setup
rate ioctl reaches a register-write leaf, not an interrupt wait
reviewed transfer helpers have no global IRQ-enable, indirect call or named wait
normal DMA read helpers have only the reviewed direct callees
vendor RX callback re-arms PDM before the indirect application callback
vendor ISR invokes its indirect callback before the DMA IRQ clear tail
first-party stop restores IRQ state before vendor stop

low-level start return is discarded by audio start
error recovery calls hardware initialization inside callback path
hardware open contains an unbounded ready-bit poll

pdm.normal_start_assessment: No software ISR wait found on the traced initialized-PDM 16 kHz path; elapsed time remains unmeasured.

open_risks.risk: An IRQ may interleave with vendor stop, and a pending old DMA IRQ may re-arm it after stop or count a completion against a new run. Channel-reset implicit IRQ-clearing semantics are not established.
Application late-callback tests do not emulate vendor ISR re-arm/ack behavior. Safe PCM ownership is not proof of stopped hardware.
Audio start discards the lower transfer return; success is not proof of active DMA. The low-level read API also returns void on its queue-full exit.
Boot initialization and FIFO-error ISR recovery can poll a peripheral ready bit without a software deadline; main-loop capture timeout cannot interrupt them.

recovery.new_asset_found: Exact-part-labelled Himax ROM-I2C bootstrap already exists in SDK; it is not a BL702 recovery image or a tested Grove recovery route.
limits: Installed 2022 BL702 source/binary not present in the inspected cache.
ROM-entry straps, external-host wiring and loader signature acceptance on this Grove are unverified.
A generic WE-I OTA guide and menu markers do not prove Grove-specific reachability, safe readback, update atomicity or successful recovery.
The SDK ota.exe default action is force-upgrade; it is not an approved diagnostic tool.

first_loader_call_order.evidence_kind: STATIC CALL-ORDER ANALYSIS OF PINNED SDK BINARY
first_loader_call_order.conclusion: In this SDK receiver, transfer ACK precedes the caller erase/program path; ACK is not burn completion or update atomicity. The caller does not inspect the program return before its done message.
limits: Installed Himax loader identity and BL702 forwarding/segmentation are unknown.
UART byte I/O uses driver function pointers; this is not an exhaustive flash-write call-graph proof.
No interrupted-transfer, power-loss, flash verification or recovery experiment was performed.
